description: Shiro Miso Soup Classic is a comforting and essential staple in Japanese cuisine, known for its delicate, slightly sweet flavor. This traditional soup, made with white miso paste and dashi broth, offers a warm, umami-rich experience that perfectly complements any meal. It is a simple yet profoundly satisfying dish enjoyed daily across Japan.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dashi Broth
instructions.text: In a medium pot, combine water and kombu. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, watching carefully to remove kombu just before the water boils to prevent bitterness. Once kombu is removed, bring the water to a rolling boil and add katsuobushi. Immediately turn off the heat and let it steep for 5-7 minutes until the bonito flakes sink to the bottom.

instructions.title: Strain the Dashi
instructions.text: Carefully strain the dashi broth through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth into a clean pot or bowl. Discard the used kombu and katsuobushi. You should have approximately 3.5 to 4 cups of clear, flavorful dashi. Set aside and keep warm.

instructions.title: Rehydrate Wakame and Prepare Tofu
instructions.text: While the dashi is steeping, place the dried wakame in a small bowl and cover with warm water for 5 minutes to rehydrate. Once softened, drain the wakame well and gently squeeze out any excess water. Cut the rehydrated wakame into smaller pieces if necessary. Dice the silken tofu into 1/2 inch cubes.

instructions.title: Add Tofu and Wakame to Dashi
instructions.text: Return the strained dashi broth to the pot and bring it to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Add the diced tofu and rehydrated wakame. Simmer gently for 2-3 minutes, allowing the tofu to warm through and the wakame to fully integrate.

instructions.title: Dissolve the Miso Paste
instructions.text: Remove a small amount of warm dashi broth (about 1/2 cup) into a separate bowl. Add the shiro miso paste to this small bowl and whisk until completely smooth and dissolved, forming a creamy paste. This prevents lumps in your soup. Reduce the heat to the lowest setting or turn it off before adding the miso.

instructions.title: Combine and Serve
instructions.text: Pour the dissolved miso mixture back into the pot with the dashi, tofu, and wakame. Stir gently to combine everything. It is crucial NOT to boil the soup after adding the miso, as this can destroy the delicate flavor and beneficial probiotics of the miso. Taste and adjust miso if needed. Ladle the hot miso soup into individual serving bowls and garnish generously with chopped green onions before serving immediately.

tips: Always remove kombu before the dashi boils to avoid a slimy texture and bitter taste.
Dissolve miso paste in a small amount of warm dashi separately before adding it to the main pot to ensure a smooth, lump-free soup.
Never boil miso soup after adding the miso paste, as high heat diminishes its delicate flavor and probiotic benefits. Simmer gently.
